name: umtx_shm_unref_reg_locked double drop of the registry reference (CVE-2024-43102)

root_cause.summary: umtx_shm_unref_reg_locked() unconditionally dropped the reference that ties a umtx_shm_reg to the global registry (USHMF_LINKED). Callers that hold umtx_shm_lock end to end are safe, but umtx_shm() releases the lock between umtx_shm_find_reg() and umtx_shm_unref_reg(true). Two threads issuing _umtx_op(UMTX_OP_SHM | UMTX_SHM_DESTROY) on the same registration can therefore both pass find_reg() and both drop the single registry reference, so the refcount reaches zero while another caller still holds a pointer and the umtx_shm_reg is freed underneath it.
root_cause.primitive: double decrement of a reference count, premature free of umtx_shm_reg, use-after-free
root_cause.trigger: two threads racing _umtx_op with UMTX_OP_SHM and the UMTX_SHM_DESTROY sub-request on the same process-shared mutex registration
root_cause.consequence: kernel panic, or use-after-free leading to arbitrary kernel read/write (the public PS5 jailbreak chains use it for exactly that)

discovery_approach.summary: Rebecca Cran filed a crash report on 2023-05-07; Synacktiv analysed the refcount handling and FreeBSD published SA-24:14 / CVE-2024-43102 with a fix on 2024-09-04. A separate write-up circulated on 2024-09-06, and PS5 ports appeared within weeks: fail0verflow built a FreeBSD-11 VM PoC and a C++ PS5 version, flatz produced the Java BD-J implementation, and Specter chained it with PSFree for PS5 1.00-5.50.
signals: a helper that drops a refcount unconditionally while one caller drops the lock before calling it
the registry link flag (USHMF_LINKED) being cleared by one thread while another still holds the object
two paths that both call unref(force=true) on the same object after a lookup
a lock window between lookup and unref in the caller

differences: the upstream fix replaces the force flag with a linked_ref parameter: only the caller that actually holds the registry reference drops it, so the object leaves umtx_shm_registry[] once and the double drop between find_reg() and unref_reg(true) is gone

PS5 8.00 is the first firmware the dev wiki lists as fixed; the FreeBSD correction is dated 2024-09-04. The fetched sources do not show the PS5 patch itself, so whether Sony took the same shape is unknown

patch_evidence.what: FreeBSD-SA-24:14.umtx and commit 62f40433ab47 ('umtx: shm: Fix use-after-free due to multiple drops of the registry reference') publish the full kern_umtx.c diff and a commit message that explains the lock drop between find_reg() and unref_reg(true)
patch_evidence.limits: this is the FreeBSD 11-era shared ancestor of the PS5 code, not the PS5 binary; the Sony backport is not public and no firmware bytes are stored here

sources.supports: concurrent UMTX_SHM_DESTROY removals decrease the mapping's reference count too many times and free it too early; impact is panic or use-after-free including code execution; CVE-2024-43102; corrected 2024-09-04

the mechanism and the fix: unref_reg_locked() unconditionally dropped the registry reference tied to USHMF_LINKED, umtx_shm() drops the lock between find_reg() and unref_reg(true), and the patch replaces force with linked_ref so the registry reference is dropped only when held
PS5 affected through 7.61 and fixed since 8.00; the fix description (decrement only if the object is still in the global array / USHMF_REG_LINKED); the list of PS5 implementations

gaps: PS4 exposure is not documented in the fetched sources; the PS4 wiki has no umtx entry, so this entry records PS5 only
the PS5 affected range lower bound is unknown (the wiki section title gives only '<= 7.61')
the exact PS5 8.00 change is not public; the FreeBSD fix is the shared ancestor, not proof of the console backport
the wiki's claim that the fix keys on USHMF_REG_LINKED is a paraphrase of the upstream commit, not an observation of PS5 code
